name: Rutilius Claudius Namatianus
credit: Part of the Tabula Peutingeriana (Konrad Miller's 1887 facsimile of the Roman road map, showing the roads of Italy); no portrait of the poet survives · Public domain (Wikimedia Commons)
bio: Rutilius Claudius Namatianus was a Gallic Roman aristocrat from the region of Toulouse. He served at Rome as master of the offices and then as prefect of the city in 414, when he was a pagan of the senatorial class writing under a Christian empire.

In 417 he left Rome to see to his estates in Gaul, which had been ravaged by the Goths, and wrote a poem in elegiac couplets, De reditu suo, about the sea voyage along the Tuscan coast. It opens with a famous hymn to Rome; the text breaks off in the second book.
